strengths.what: One CTA wording (Start free) everywhere, with the no card / no contract line right under it
strengths.why: Removes the main trial objection at the moment of click. Keep the single action.

strengths.what: The compare table names the typical booking app and shows row by row why Meikigo differs
strengths.why: Honest unlike framing a shop owner can check against Fresha. Keep it.

strengths.what: Full RM pricing on the page with tiers, limits and a yearly toggle
strengths.why: SMB owners want the number before signing up. Transparency builds trust.

strengths.what: The FAQ tackles Fresha, setup time, devices, payments and cancellation
strengths.why: Answers the real switching objections before the closing CTA.

recommendations.opportunity: Put the real product (tablet queue board or phone booking #42) in the hero instead of the photo alone
recommendations.why: A cold visitor sees a haircut, not software. The product appears only after scrolling past the problem section.

recommendations.opportunity: Replace the two unverified shop quotes and the pilot note with honest early-access proof
recommendations.why: Unverifiable shop names plus a visible "quotes come next" note read as placeholder proof. They also break the no-invented-proof rule in MESSAGING.md.

recommendations.opportunity: Restore concrete shop pains in the problem section (walk-ins vs bookings, WhatsApp bookings, commissions counted at close)
recommendations.why: One abstract line does not make an owner feel the problem. The concrete beats already exist in data.ts but are commented out.

recommendations.opportunity: Make the H1 or sub state the difference from booking apps (booking, queue, payment and report on one tablet)
recommendations.why: The manifesto H1 could fit any salon tool. The sharpest differentiator only appears in the problem line and compare table.

recommendations.opportunity: Raise contrast on the hero sub, trial line and trust ticker
recommendations.why: White text on the light beige photo makes the risk reducer and trust signals hard to read.

recommendations.opportunity: Replace "Plus-equivalent trial" with plain wording that matches the promo banner
recommendations.why: The banner says 14-day free trial, the hero says Plus-equivalent trial. A new visitor does not know what Plus is yet.

recommendations.opportunity: Say what happens after Start free (create the shop, get the door QR, take the first booking)
recommendations.why: Owners hesitate when the next step is unknown. A one-line next step near the CTA lowers that risk.

recommendations.opportunity: Use one setup-time claim across the page
recommendations.why: Under five minutes, live by afternoon and setup in one afternoon all appear. Conflicting numbers weaken each other.

recommendations.opportunity: Add a low-commitment option next to Start free, such as a short queue walkthrough video
recommendations.why: Some owners want to see the counter flow before creating an account. Today the only path is signup.

recommendations.opportunity: Give every pricing card the same CTA colour and a trial reminder under the button
recommendations.why: Starter and Pro buttons are black while Plus is lime. No card repeats that the trial is free with no card.

recommendations.opportunity: Swap the problem-section imagery for a Malaysian shop context (RM prices, local signage)
recommendations.why: The current image shows $ prices and French signage. That undercuts "Made for Malaysian barbershops".

recommendations.opportunity: Show the payment rails the product supports (DuitNow QR, card networks) as marks in the trust bar
recommendations.why: Recognisable payment marks add credibility without claiming shop counts.

recommendations.opportunity: Fix the FAQ sub "Answers to your question" to plural
recommendations.why: Small grammar slips near the decision point chip at polish.

recommendations.opportunity: Add FAQ or How it works to the nav and group footer links under labels
recommendations.why: Three nav links and one flat footer row make it harder to jump to answers.

pageLevel.opportunity: Move the compare table up to sit right after the problem section
pageLevel.why: The problem line sets up "booking apps stop at the appointment". The proof of that claim sits five sections later.

pageLevel.opportunity: Demote the H1 tags inside the product mock screens to non-heading elements
pageLevel.why: The page renders four H1s (hero plus mock screens). One H1 keeps the heading outline and SEO signal clean.

sectorSpecific.opportunity: Name WhatsApp bookings explicitly as the pain Meikigo replaces
sectorSpecific.why: Malaysian shops run bookings through WhatsApp. The persona page never mentions it (judgment, not the rubric).

sectorSpecific.opportunity: Add a line for multi-outlet chains and unisex salons pointing at Pro
sectorSpecific.why: The ICP includes chains and salons, but the page speaks only to single barbershops (judgment, not the rubric).

sectorSpecific.opportunity: State plainly that payments settle to the shop's own DuitNow and bank account
sectorSpecific.why: Who holds the money is a top trust question for Malaysian SMB owners (judgment, not the rubric).
